question: The objective of the "Gadgil Formula," introduced during the Fourth Five Year Plan, was to allocate plan assistance to states based on their:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Population and per capita income**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Gadgil Formula was introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969–1974) to allocate plan assistance from the Central Government to states in India.
 
• Its objective was to ensure a balanced regional development by considering various socio-economic factors.
 
• Key Parameters of the Gadgil Formula:
 
• Population (60% weight): States with larger populations were allocated more funds.
 
• Per Capita Income (25% weight): Special attention was given to states with lower per capita income to reduce regional disparities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other parameters
 
 
• Performance (7.5% weight): States were evaluated based on their performance in plan implementation.
 
• Special Problems (7.5% weight): Specific issues unique to states, such as natural calamities, were also considered.
 
• The formula aimed to prioritize equity by directing more resources to states with a lower per capita income.
 
• It ensured that states with larger populations received adequate resources to address their developmental needs.
